set.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Clean Living begins on a vertical crack system about midway between Taphophobia and Fear of Flying, on the gently overhanging orange face.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

Delta Crucis is on the southwest face and is one of the westernmost full-length routes, around the corner to the right of The Astraphobia Treatment, and lower on the hillside than the short route that climbs the pillar farther right. It begins in the white groove and aims for the right side of the big headwall.

set.descent_text: The climbing turns to a scramble among pines on the arete. Belay in the pines at the sandy spot and walk off to climber's right.

From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. The Astraphobia Treatment is at the right end of the south face, where a wide crack system rises rightward to a triangular pinnacle; start at its foot.
set.descent_text: From the summit, follow the ridge, which is exposed and easy, until sand, talus and slabs make it possible to descend back to the base on either the east or the west side.

set.approach: Drive forest road 2N13 and then 2N13D to their junction and park; a climbers trail goes up the ramp above the gully, and a steep bushy scramble leads on to the pinnacle's southwest side. Crack 1742 is a short crack just round the corner, right of Napoleon Syndrome.

set.approach: Pull off on the outer edge of Tioga Road right under the formation and climb the shattered slabs above the road to the base, or start from the Warren Creek trailhead at the unofficial campground on the bend in US 120. The line follows the east ridge, which can be joined at the saddle reached from the back side, or traversed in full from Warren Creek, a loose option.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Take the McGee Creek trail up McGee Creek Canyon, and before the side trail east to Steelhead Lake, fork right onto the old mining road into Baldwin Canyon. Follow it until the pillar comes into view on the left. The route is the clear crack splitting the middle of the pillar.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Angels and Demons climbs the middle buttress, down and left of Friends; look for the pillar with a rappel anchor and the flake crack to its left.
set.descent_text: Scramble off, or rappel the route: every belay is bolted, and the first rappel runs from the second anchor straight down to a pedestal and then the ground.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Climb the talus to the wall's lowest point, where a square-cut corner system facing right rises off the ground. Friends climbs the face and cracks just to its right, just left of the other established routes.
set.descent_text: Either rappel the line using the fixed anchors, starting from the top of the last roped pitch, or walk off from the summit.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Spring Roll takes the leftmost of the three formations, starting at its toe up a right-facing layback corner.
set.descent_text: Go left over the back of the formation toward Cyclamen Lake; a steep gully on the way may need a short rappel from a slung boulder. Keep angling left and down the slabs to return to Spring Lake. Alternatively, go on to the top of the main formation and use its descent.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Park at St. Marys Pass and hike to the top, then head north toward Stanislaus Peak. The top of the crag is a long way out, and a safe line down to the base can be hard to find. The route is the pillar standing in the gully's midline, close to where a party would rappel in.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: From the Mosquito Flat trailhead, follow the Little Lakes Valley Trail beyond Chickenfoot Lake. A little past the lake, before the turnoff for Morgan Pass, the trail crosses the creek on stepping stones, and the crag is right beside the crossing. Daisies Dihedral is the largest dihedral on the wall.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: From the Mosquito Flat trailhead, follow the Little Lakes Valley Trail beyond Chickenfoot Lake. A little past the lake, before the turnoff for Morgan Pass, the trail crosses the creek on stepping stones, and the crag is right beside the crossing. Stepping Stone Crack is the clear full-height crack on the main face, immediately left of the biggest dihedral.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Follow the approach to Indian Buttress, then continue up into Echo Gully; the Wall of Echos is the big steep cliff band on the immediate left. A climbers trail runs along its base if you stay to the extreme left just after the Little Indian. Land Animal climbs a crack that starts uphill of Swooped, running up to a small roof.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. From the ledge with the anchor shared with Rain Shadow, it is easier to rappel Rain Shadow than to continue down Land Animal.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Follow the approach to Indian Buttress, then continue up into Echo Gully; the Wall of Echos is the big steep cliff band on the immediate left. A climbers trail runs along its base if you stay to the extreme left just after the Little Indian. The Wrong Hill follows a splitter crack that starts a little way uphill from where the trail touches the cliff; the first pitch is a hand crack to a large pine tree.
set.descent_text: Stay roped and belayed and walk a short way east to the summit. Below, the anchor of Swooped sits on a small ledge, and the rappel from it is exposed; rappel Swooped to the ground.

set.approach: Hike up to the south face of the Rectory and go east, then find a way across; the line goes high past the Rectory south face and up second-class ground toward the Rectory east face, then past the Convent and Mosque notch. Direct routes through oak and mahogany are possible but thick. The route tracks a steep water streak toward the right side of the Synagogue's west face, and begins with an unprotected easy slab to a ledge.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. Table Top Rock is a small block uphill and west of Secret Spot Rock. Pinch It and Leave It is on the right side of the south face, starting off a boulder to a prominent flake.

set.approach: Park in the northwest-facing turnout on the north side of the road east of Holcomb Valley Campground; the south-facing granite slab is visible from the road a short walk north. Canon is the offwidth just right of Enterprise.

set.approach: Park at the hairpin turn and follow the Coven trail north across the first ridge and the seasonal stream bed on the way up to the Dragonlance and Voodoo walls. About midway up the gully you reach the Addams Family slab on your left. Pugsley is the crack on the right side of the slab.
set.descent_text: Walk off by scrambling down the left (west) side of the slab.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the wall page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: In Sequoia National Park, start up the Paradise Ridge trail from the trailhead by Atwell Mill campground, along the Mineral King road, and climb it to the ridge. Leave the trail there and travel cross-country north-northwest, contouring across small drainages, until the wall and the gully beneath it appear. Keep to the gully's east side until you are under the wall, then cross over and go up to the base. The Sage is on the south face. From the bivy site, work left around the wall and slightly upward over dirt ledges to the foot of the first left-facing corner, which lies down and right of the large corner where the pillar joins the main face.
set.descent_text: The route tops out on a pseudo-summit with no downclimb back to the rest of the formation. Rappel from bolts into the notch, scramble the blocky ridge to the true summit, then rappel from there and descend clockwise back to camp.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.
